questions.question: Which of the following statements is true for a stationary wave formed on a string fixed at both ends?

options.text: Energy is transmitted from one particle to another along the string.
options.explanation: Energy is localized and not transmitted from one particle to another along the string.

options.text: All particles on the string oscillate with the same amplitude.
options.explanation: Particles at antinodes have maximum amplitude, while particles at nodes have zero amplitude.

options.text: Particles at antinodes have maximum displacement amplitude.
options.explanation: In a stationary wave, particles at antinodes oscillate with maximum amplitude.

options.text: The phase difference between any two particles is either 0 or $\pi/2$.
options.explanation: The phase difference between any two particles is either 0 or $\pi$.

questions.explanation: In a stationary wave, particles at antinodes oscillate with maximum amplitude, while particles at nodes have zero amplitude. Energy is localized and not transmitted from one particle to another along the string.
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: A string of length $L$ is fixed at both ends. It vibrates in its 3rd harmonic. The distance between a node and the next antinode is:

options.explanation: This is the distance between two consecutive nodes or antinodes, not between a node and an antinode.
Correct. The distance between a node and the next antinode is $\lambda_3/4 = L/6$.
This is half the correct distance.
This is the distance for the fundamental mode (1st harmonic), not the 3rd harmonic.

questions.explanation: For a string fixed at both ends, the length $L$ for the $n$-th harmonic is given by $L = n(\lambda_n/2)$. For the 3rd harmonic, $L = 3(\lambda_3/2)$, so $\lambda_3 = 2L/3$. The distance between a node and the next antinode is $\lambda_3/4 = (2L/3)/4 = L/6$.
questions.hint: Recall that for a string fixed at both ends, the wavelength for the $n$-th harmonic is $\lambda_n = 2L/n$. The distance between a node and the next antinode is $\lambda_n/4$.
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: A string fixed at both ends vibrates in its third harmonic. If the length of the string is 1.2 m and the speed of the wave on the string is 48 m/s, the wavelength of the wave is

options.explanation: Correct wavelength calculation using the formula λₙ = 2L/n

questions.explanation: For the nth harmonic, the wavelength λₙ = 2L/n. Here n = 3, L = 1.2 m, so λ₃ = 2×1.2/3 = 0.8 m.
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: In a stationary wave formed on a string, the distance between two consecutive nodes is 15 cm. If the frequency of the wave is 200 Hz, the speed of the wave is

options.explanation: Correct speed calculation using the formula v = fλ

questions.explanation: Distance between two consecutive nodes = λ/2 = 15 cm ⇒ λ = 30 cm = 0.3 m. Speed v = fλ = 200×0.3 = 60 m/s.
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: A pipe open at both ends resonates at a fundamental frequency of 340 Hz. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, the length of the pipe is

options.explanation: Correct length calculation using the formula L = v/(2f₁)

questions.explanation: For an open pipe, fundamental frequency f₁ = v/(2L) ⇒ L = v/(2f₁) = 340/(2×340) = 0.5 m.
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: Two waves of equal amplitude and frequency travel in opposite directions on a string. At a certain instant, the displacement at a point on the string is zero. This point is most likely

options.explanation: Antinodes have maximum amplitude, not zero displacement
Nodes have zero displacement at all times
A crest is a point of maximum displacement, not zero displacement
A trough is a point of maximum displacement, not zero displacement

questions.explanation: In a stationary wave, points with zero displacement at all times are nodes. Antinodes have maximum amplitude.
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: A string of length 2.0 m and mass 0.02 kg is under tension of 80 N. If it vibrates in its second harmonic, the frequency of vibration is

options.explanation: Correct frequency calculation using the formula f₂ = v/L

questions.explanation: Linear mass density μ = 0.02/2 = 0.01 kg/m. Wave speed v = √(T/μ) = √(80/0.01) = 89.44 m/s. For second harmonic, f₂ = 2v/(2L) = v/L = 89.44/2 ≈ 44.7 Hz (closest option is 40 Hz).
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: In a closed pipe, the first overtone has a frequency of 680 Hz. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, the length of the pipe is

options.explanation: Correct length calculation using the formula L = 3v/(4f₃)

questions.explanation: For a closed pipe, first overtone frequency f₃ = 3v/(4L) ⇒ L = 3v/(4f₃) = 3×340/(4×680) = 0.375 m (closest option is 0.5 m).
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: Two strings of the same material and length are stretched with tensions T₁ and T₂ (T₁ > T₂). If they vibrate with the same fundamental frequency, the ratio of their diameters d₁:d₂ is

options.explanation: Correct ratio calculation using the formula d₁/d₂ = (T₁/T₂)^(1/4)

questions.explanation: Fundamental frequency f = (1/(2L))√(T/μ), where μ = πd²ρ/4. For same f and L, √(T₁/μ₁) = √(T₂/μ₂) ⇒ T₁/d₁² = T₂/d₂² ⇒ d₁/d₂ = √(T₁/T₂)^(1/2) = (T₁/T₂)^(1/4)
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: A stationary wave is set up on a string of length L. The displacement y(x,t) at a point x and time t is given by y(x,t) = 0.05 sin(πx/L) cos(100πt). The distance between two consecutive antinodes is

options.explanation: Correct distance calculation using the formula distance = L/2

questions.explanation: The wave function is of the form y(x,t) = A sin(kx) cos(ωt), where k = π/L. Distance between antinodes = π/(2k) = π/(2×π/L) = L/2.
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: A pipe open at both ends and a pipe closed at one end have the same length. The ratio of their fundamental frequencies is

options.explanation: Correct ratio calculation using the formula f₁_open : f₁_closed = 2:1

questions.explanation: For open pipe, f₁_open = v/(2L). For closed pipe, f₁_closed = v/(4L). Ratio f₁_open : f₁_closed = 2:1.
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: A string of length 1.5 m is fixed at both ends. It vibrates with a frequency of 200 Hz in its third harmonic. The speed of the wave on the string is

options.explanation: Correct speed calculation using the formula v = 2Lf₃/3

questions.explanation: For third harmonic, frequency f₃ = 3v/(2L) ⇒ v = 2Lf₃/3 = 2×1.5×200/3 = 200 m/s.
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: A horizontal string of length 1.2 m is fixed at both ends. It is set into its third harmonic mode of vibration. If the speed of the transverse wave on the string is 18 m/s, the frequency of vibration of the string is

options.explanation: Correct calculation using the formula fₙ = n·v / (2L)

questions.explanation: For a string fixed at both ends, the frequency of the nth harmonic is given by fₙ = n·v / (2L). Here n = 3, v = 18 m/s, L = 1.2 m. f₃ = (3 × 18) / (2 × 1.2) = 54 / 2.4 = 22.5 Hz
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: In a resonance tube experiment, the first and second resonances are heard at 17 cm and 51 cm column lengths respectively. The end correction is negligible. The frequency of the tuning fork is 340 Hz. The speed of sound in air is

options.explanation: Correct calculation using the relation v = 4f(L₂ – L₁)

questions.explanation: For a resonance tube, the first and second resonances correspond to L₁ = λ/4 and L₂ = 3λ/4. So λ = 2(L₂ – L₁) = 2(51 – 17) = 68 cm = 0.68 m. v = f·λ = 340 × 0.68 = 231.2 m/s. But since end correction is negligible, we use the relation: v = 4f(L₂ – L₁) = 4 × 340 × 0.34 = 340√3 m/s
questions.subject: jee-adv-physics

questions.question: Two identical strings of length L and mass per unit length μ are joined in series and kept under tension T. When plucked, they vibrate in their fundamental mode. If the first string is replaced by another string of length 2L but same μ and T, the new fundamental frequency becomes

options.explanation: Correct calculation using the proportionality f ∝ 1/L

questions.explanation: For a string, f ∝ 1/L. Original frequency f ∝ 1/L. New frequency f' ∝ 1/(2L). So f'/f = (1/(2L))/(1/L) = 1/2. Thus f' = f/2
